No capacity check in Tasks::Decode, Base::Decode, EnsureMtpDrafterLoaded or Draft. Verify input_pos = position+i, i<4. Primed: step = GetStep = c-1. Priming: Draft(current_step-1) after DecodeLogitsImpl incremented, = c. Primed c<=N-1 -> p+3<=N+1; priming after full prefill c<=N -> c+3<=N+3.

Kernel non-ring branch: token_index = params[0]+X, return if >= cache_size or >= params[1]. Both parsers (classic and ir) use CreateAddValuesToCacheFromNode; e4b-ours cache_update attrs cache_size 32003, no is_ring_buffer; magic_number_utils rewrites int attributes of odml.cache_update. params[1] = start+4, so cache_size does the bounding.

PrepareVerifierInputBuffers calls FillAttentionMask(position, 4 steps, global_type) unconditionally (both builds); no executor metadata section in the file, default CAUSAL; row k fills offset kN..kN+p+k+1, no clamp. Overrun p+4-N: primed p<=N-2 gives <=2, priming p<=N gives <=4 bytes (BOOL).

tensor_buffer.cc: posix_memalign(size + XNN_EXTRA_BYTES), tail memset 0; XNN_EXTRA_BYTES 16 under LITERT_DISABLE_CPU. The host-memory fallback is LiteRT's (GetTensorBufferRequirements in compiled_model.cc), not a LiteRT-LM CreateInputBuffer; the cited LiteRT-LM lines are a comment describing it.
corrected_text: Where the verify-mask overrun lands depends on the mask's buffer: when no GPU consumer registers requirements for a BOOL mask, LiteRT's compiled model (362759838) falls back to host-memory requirements, so the CreateInputBuffer call LiteRT-LM makes returns a host buffer, which LiteRT allocates with posix_memalign of the buffer size plus XNN_EXTRA_BYTES and zero-fills that tail (XNN_EXTRA_BYTES is 16 when LiteRT is built without its CPU path, XNNPACK's own value otherwise); which buffer type the verify mask gets on Metal, and what a write past a Metal buffer's tensor size hits, were not traced.

SendMessage passes ToMessage's StatusOr to user_callback, stream continues; ResponseTextToMessage with preface tools -> ParseTextAndToolCalls -> InvalidArgument when return_error_on_parse_failure (default true; not set in c/ or swift/ either build). Both wrappers: streamCallback takeUnretainedValue, then release on any error chunk regardless of isFinal, and on final (direct or in tool Task). sendMessageStream's local context only passed via passRetained; StreamContext not captured elsewhere once the closure returns. Second error chunk reads freed context and releases again.

SendCompleteMessage returns after extraction/ToMessage error without Message(); internal callback error, cancelled, failed and max-token-error branches each call user_callback once and return (both builds). Pin: refill error paths call shared_user_callback with error while defer_completion stays true, so wrapped_user_callback drops the sentinel.

In both wrappers the catch around JSONSerialization/jsonToMessage finishes the continuation, releases the context and returns, with no cancel of the native stream; subsequent chunks call takeUnretainedValue on the released context.

ComputeNext calls llg_commit_token on state's pointer and returns make_unique<LlgState>(llg_state), a copy sharing the shared_ptr<LlgConstraintOwner>; the only llg_clone_constraint is in Start(). Same in 85b1a776.

RunDraftingLoop: mask from current_draft_state, then ComputeNext commits draft into the shared matcher; RunVerification computes masks from constraint_state_ and the three draft states, all the same matcher after d3, applied per verifier row. Same in v0.18.0. (Exception only if IsEnded resets to Start mid-draft.)

Draft: constraint_state_ = draft_states[n-1] when n>0 (unchanged, same matcher, when n=0), then ComputeNext(bonus) commits on the matcher holding d1..d3; llg_commit_token failure returns InternalError 'Failed to commit token: ...'. Same in v0.18.0 (826-849).

DecodeLogitsImpl reads ran_decode before PrepareFirstDecode and calls UpdateState only if last run was decode; masks with ConstrainedDecoder's own states. Draft with activations resets constraint_state_ = Start(), ComputeMask, ComputeNext(token_id). Only other UpdateState callers: Tasks external-sampler path, NPU and fake executors.

Code supports grammar-violating output: drafts are masked from correct sequential states, but verifier rows 0-2 use the after-d3 mask, so a rejection's bonus can violate the grammar and rejected drafts stay committed. Agello's comment attributes the bug to drafted tokens bypassing the mask; the code shows drafts are masked, so 'matches' overstates.
corrected_text: Consequence: with speculative decoding on and an llguidance constraint (a JSON schema or a regex response format), the documented build and the v0.18.0 source can emit tokens the grammar doesn't allow: the drafts are masked from the right states, but a rejection's bonus token is picked under the mask of the position after d3, and a rejected draft stays committed in the matcher, so later masks come from a wrong state; this is consistent with the symptoms Agello recorded on device (garbled output or "compute_mask() called after stop", LM-SWIFT-059), though Agello's comment blames the drafted tokens, so MTP must stay off for constrained conversations at the pin too, and it is a correctness bug to report upstream.

note: outputCap: room = max - used - input - 64, nil if <96; free >= input+160 >= ceil(L/128)*128. But the window is Agello's maxNumTokens: a manual KV size of 32,768 (Stepper up to maxContextTokens 32,768; E4B caps 0) allocates 32,000, voiding the margin. With tools the cap is room/4.
corrected_text: Agello (93122b6) starts a chat reply only when maxNumTokens minus the tokens in use, the input estimate and a 64-token margin leaves at least 96 tokens, and caps the reply at that room (at a quarter of it when tools are offered). When maxNumTokens is below 32,003, so that it equals E4B's allocated context (the defaults 8,192 and 4,096 are), and with exact counts, a send's prefill then has at least its input plus 160 positions free, more than the at most input + 127 that E4B's prefill_128 runs need, and a reply without tool calls stops decoding 64 positions before the end of the window plus at most one MTP round's tokens, so it stays clear of the positions an MTP round can reach past the end. A manual KV-cache size of 32,768 (the Stepper's top when the app memory limit reads at least 6.5 GB) allocates only 32,000 positions, and the margin no longer holds.
